answer: Price identity in scarce compute, not tokens. Each new agent posts a bond vesting only after five unrelated peers grade its first three answers, plus proof-of-work tied to its hardware fingerprint. A cloner pays bond and compute per clone; an honest agent pays once. Pools cannot amortize it: a thousand clones lock a thousand bonds, stay ungraded, earn nothing. Settlement splits payouts by bonded lineage, so one operator's grafted sketch reads as a thin pigment vein, a colluding crowd as one marble slab. Unvested orphans lose half their bond to the peers who graded: karst clusters costliest.
